classification.difficultyReason: Use two corresponding angle equalities to establish similarity and derive an equal half on the remaining side.

content.prompt: Prove that the line through the midpoint of one side of a triangle parallel to another side meets the third side of the triangle at its midpoint.

spec.description: M is midpointAB, MNparallelAC crossesBCatN. OnlyAM/MB ticks marked; BN/NC equality is to be proved.
spec.mathematics: M is midpointAB, MNparallelAC crossesBCatN. OnlyAM/MB ticks marked; BN/NC equality is to be proved.
spec.answerVisibility: Original givens only; no answer values added.

answer.short: N is the midpoint of BC.
answer.worked: Let M be the midpoint of AB and let $MN\parallel AC$, with N on BC. Corresponding angles give $\angle BMN=\angle BAC$ and $\angle BNM=\angle BCA$, so $\triangle BMN\sim\triangle BAC$ by AAA. Thus $\frac{BN}{BC}=\frac{BM}{BA}=\frac{1}{2}$, giving $BN=\frac{BC}{2}=NC$. Hence N is the midpoint of BC.
